analysis.title: Bonds Haven't Noticed Yet: Citadel Securities Spots Record 3.5-Sigma Gap Between Yields And Growth
key_insights: Citadel's new Cross-Market Internals Growth factor (X-MIG) sits at -1.85 standard deviations on a 1-year rolling basis, down from a +2σ peak mid-year. That is a near 4-sigma round trip in about six months.

Nine of ten X-MIG inputs contributed negatively over three months, for a cumulative 18-point drop. Equity sector leadership, small caps, credit risk appetite, FX risk appetite and industrial commodities are all lower. Metals was the lone holdout and also faded last month.

The 10Y yield sits at +1.75σ on the same z-score basis, a gap of more than 3.5 sigma versus X-MIG. Flight calls this historically large. Comparable spikes came in late 2018, 2022, late 2023 and early 2025.

Inflation and the Fed, not growth, are driving duration. Citadel expects consecutive Fed hikes starting in December. Goldman added a third hike after hot October CPI and Waller floating a 50bps December hike.

Citadel expects damage to show first through a flatter yield curve and tighter US financial conditions. The 2s10s beta to growth pricing was positive in 2017-18 and 2021-22 hiking cycles and should reassert itself.

AI capex circularity: capex across nine cloud providers is estimated to rise from $465B in 2025 to $957B this year, +$492B or about 1.42% of US nominal GDP. Citadel's 2027 estimate of $1.5T implies a $543B increment, about 1.41% of GDP. Growth slows from +106% to +57%.

AI capex is estimated to add about 0.55-0.56pp to 2027 nominal GDP growth, roughly flat vs this year, assuming 60% import leakage. Fading OBBBA impulse and tighter financial conditions net to about a 0.35% growth drag in 2027.

Political risk to the buildout: electoral backlash against data centers could delay construction. Bernstein reckons only 199GW of the 586GW forward pipeline is credible. Open-weight models and falling token prices squeeze frontier lab margins.

S&P 500 slid back below its 200-day moving average and was on track for a sixth straight decline despite a strong Nvidia quarter and a large IPO. Goldman's Privorotsky said nothing good happens below the 200-day. Nomura's McElligott said 'somebody wants out.'
The author argues internals are right and the index is late. In the last two episodes of such a gap during hiking cycles (late 2018 and 2022), stocks caught down to the internals.

sector_views.rationale: X-MIG internals show cyclicals, small caps and credit risk appetite weakening, pointing to downside growth risk.

earnings_insights: Street expects roughly 16% earnings growth for 2027 (consensus), which Citadel says clashes with the growth signal from market internals.
Nvidia's most recent quarter was described as a blowout, but the S&P still fell below its 200-day moving average.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Internals are pricing a growth slowdown well below index and data levels.
Yields are near highs on inflation and Fed, diverging from growth pricing.
Historically large gap. Prior episodes resolved with equities catching down.
Supported hawkish Fed repricing and Goldman adding a third hike.

macro_indicators.reading: consecutive hikes starting December (Citadel), Waller floated 50bps in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: Fed tightening into a growth scare supports curve flattening.
Growth in the increment slows, so the second derivative turns negative.

trade_ideas.description: Position for a flatter US yield curve (2s10s flattening) as hot inflation and a hawkish Fed pin the front end while weaker growth pulls down long yields
trade_ideas.rationale: Beta of 2s10s to growth pricing turned positive in prior hiking cycles and should reassert itself.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth resilience from AI capex persists and long yields keep rising on inflation.

risk_factors: Fed hiking into a slowdown that internals say has already started.
Heavy dependence of US growth on a single AI capex cycle.
Data center political veto and construction delays.
Frontier lab margin pressure from open-weight models and collapsing token prices.
Fading fiscal support (OBBBA) and tighter financial conditions, about a 0.35% growth drag in 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: The economy and index look fine, and AI capex-driven resilience has kept the AI unwind from becoming a broad growth scare.
tension_points.bear_case: X-MIG at -1.85σ with nine of ten inputs negative, capex growth halving, data center political risk and a Fed hiking into slowdown point to equities catching down.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Internals recovering, such as X-MIG rebounding toward the 10Y z-score, or AI capex proving more durable than Citadel expects.
